clue.text: Doctor's job forces leader to behave when in charge

parts.note: a general is a commander of armed forces

indicators.note: the behaving word sits inside the word for charge

parts.note: a charge is the price asked for something
to act is to behave in a certain way

explanation.surface: A doctor's work involves forcing a commander to behave while he is in charge of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like being in command, the general's role; here it means a cost.
explanation.definitionFit: A family doctor in Britain works in a surgery offering general medical care, the work of a GP.

clue.text: Youngster requires energy drink

parts.note: go means energy or vigour
a sling is a cocktail of spirit, sugar and water, as in the Singapore variety

explanation.surface: A young person needs an energy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A young goose is called by this word, so it means a youngster in the bird world.

clue.text: One makes points to goad Republican

parts.note: to needle someone is to goad or provoke them

explanation.surface: Someone scores points by goading a Republican politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who needles makes pointed, sharp jibes; one who makes points in a teasing way.

clue.text: Do truer discoing possibly from its output?

definitions.text: Do truer discoing possibly from its output?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the words before it could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Asks whether more authentic dancing might come from what a certain place produces.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both anagram and definition: disco music played in clubs is the output of the place being described.
explanation.definitionFit: A soundproofed room where music is recorded produces the tracks people dance to at a disco.

clue.text: Outsider has hot pants the wrong way round

indicators.note: the two words in 'hot pants' are taken in the opposite order to the one printed

parts.note: longs are long trousers, and pants means trousers in American usage
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unlikely contender is wearing their hot pants back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way round' swaps the two words, not the letters: pants comes first, then hot.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner with little chance of winning, an outsider, is described as this in betting.

clue.text: Like newly turfed pitch? Spinning bowler not half needs supporting help

indicators.note: in a down entry the help word sits beneath the first part, holding it up
spinning turns the remaining letters round to read backwards
remove half of the six-letter word bowler, its first three letters

parts.note: the clue word itself, from which half is removed
aid means help

explanation.surface: A cricket picture: a spin bowler, struggling, needs backing on a freshly turfed pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' drops BOW from bowler, leaving LER; 'Spinning' turns that to REL.
explanation.definitionFit: Turf that has been put down again has been laid a second time, as on a freshly re-turfed pitch.

clue.text: Botanic Prof torn suffering damage to environment?

indicators.note: the torn and suffering letters are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A botany professor, ripped apart and in pain, causes harm to the environment.
explanation.definitionFit: This measure of greenhouse gases a person or activity emits is the harm they do to the environment.

clue.text: What some churches use to arouse passion

definitions.meaning: fragrant resin burned in services, especially Catholic and Orthodox
as a verb it means to make very angry or enrage

explanation.surface: Churches using something to stir up feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Burned aromatic resin in worship; as a verb, stressed on the second syllable, it means to inflame with anger.

clue.text: Back last runner at 'Aydock?

parts.note: the end is the last part
a horse runs at Haydock racecourse; dropping the H in 'Aydock signals the dropped H of the runner too

explanation.surface: Backing the last-placed horse at Haydock, said in a dropped-H accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Haydock is a racecourse in north-west England; the missing H mimics a regional accent.
explanation.definitionFit: To support or give approval to something is to back it; one also signs on the back of a cheque.

clue.text: Casual zen deployed in part of Passage to India

indicators.note: deployed means spread out or arranged, so the letters are set out in another order

explanation.surface: Relaxed Zen ideas spread through part of E. M. Forster's novel A Passage to India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage to India' looks like the novel, but means the shipping route from Europe to India.
explanation.definitionFit: The Egyptian waterway linking the Mediterranean and Red Sea forms part of the sea route to India.

clue.text: Expert in road went fast

indicators.note: the expert word goes inside the road abbreviation

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A skilled driver on the road drove quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Raced is the past tense of race, to move at speed, so it matches went fast.

clue.text: Good-for-nothing makes Bette lose her head

indicators.note: her first letter, the start of her surname, is dropped

parts.note: Bette Midler is an American singer and actress

explanation.surface: A layabout causes the star Bette to lose her temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy person who does no work is a ne'er-do-well, a good-for-nothing.

clue.text: Transport magnate's shown ripe bananas

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A shipping tycoon displays bananas that are ripe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like the fruit being shown; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tycoon who owns vessels is a magnate in the transport of goods by sea.

clue.text: Fortification arranged by having US soldiers coming round working

indicators.note: the soldiers surround the abbreviation for arranged

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
ARR is the abbreviation for arranged, as in music credits
on means working or operating

explanation.surface: A fort is arranged by having American troops going around it in action.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of troops stationed to defend a place, or the fortified post itself.

clue.text: Swear summer in Cannes makes you exhausted

parts.note: to eff is to swear, from the euphemism for the F-word
ete is the French word for summer

explanation.surface: Cursing the Riviera summer heat leaves you worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Effete means feeble and worn out, having lost its former vigour.

clue.text: Criminal, German, concealing disquiet

indicators.note: the German abbreviation hides the disquiet word inside it

parts.note: angst is anxiety or disquiet

explanation.surface: A German crook hiding his unease.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an organised gang of violent crooks is a criminal.

clue.text: Venetian leader receives thanks in declining years

indicators.note: the leader takes in the thanks word

parts.note: the doge was the elected ruler of the Venetian republic
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: An ageing Venetian ruler is thanked in his old age.
explanation.definitionFit: Old age, especially with failing mental powers, is the period of declining years.

clue.text: Detective workers on woman's side

parts.note: DI is Detective Inspector
staff are the workers in an organisation

explanation.surface: A detective's staff are working on behalf of a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The distaff side of a family is the female line, named after the spinning staff.

clue.text: Track laid round area — very hard work

indicators.note: the track word is placed around the two abbreviations

parts.note: a trail is a track

explanation.surface: A path is laid around a district; it is very tough labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'very' looks part of the definition, but gives V.
explanation.definitionFit: Travail is painful or laborious effort, from the old French word for toil.

clue.text: American wrestler hiding in one tree or another

indicators.note: the wrestler is tucked inside the tree word

parts.note: may is the hawthorn tree
Hulk Hogan is a famous American wrestler

explanation.surface: An American grappler takes cover in a tree of one kind or other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' stands for a second tree, a tropical hardwood.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahogany is a tropical hardwood timber, so it is another tree beside the hawthorn.

clue.text: Molten rock goes skywards carrying aluminium alloy in liquid form

indicators.note: the reversed rock holds the metal symbol inside
in a down entry, going up reverses the letters

parts.note: magma is molten rock below the earth's surface
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: Lava shoots upward carrying aluminium in a molten alloy.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixture of mercury with another metal, often soft or fluid, as used in dental fillings.

clue.text: Dairy products sort guy out

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Products from the dairy sort out a bloke.
explanation.definitionFit: Fermented milk products, such as the cultured ones in pots, are dairy items.

clue.text: Put a stop to glitch so bike keeps up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read backwards
the words keep the letters tucked away inside them

explanation.surface: A fault stops things, so a bicycle stays upright.
explanation.definitionFit: To put the kibosh on something is an idiom for halting or ending it.

clue.text: Scaring bird round top of tree

indicators.note: the bird is placed around one letter

parts.note: the starling is a common bird

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Frightening a bird perched round the top of a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Something alarming or surprising startles, so startling means scaring.

clue.text: Crash has queen in pain

indicators.note: the queen letter goes inside the pain word

parts.note: a pang is a sudden sharp pain
R is from Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A collision leaves the monarch in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: Prang is British slang for a crash, especially a car or aircraft collision.

clue.text: A lottery returned prize

indicators.note: returned means the lottery word reads backwards

parts.note: a draw is a lottery

explanation.surface: A lottery gave back a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Something given for achievement is an honour or prize.

clue.text: Dark Blues briefly set off in racing boat

parts.note: the Dark Blues are Oxford's rowing crew; briefly, Oxford University is OU
to trigger is to set off

explanation.surface: The Oxford rowers began their race in a racing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dark Blues are Oxford in the Boat Race against Cambridge, the Light Blues.
explanation.definitionFit: A light racing boat with rowlocks on projecting brackets is called by this name.

clue.text: Suffer poverty cultivating hostile farmland

indicators.note: cultivating means working the soil, turning the letters over into a new order

explanation.surface: Farming land that is unforgiving leaves one impoverished.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for becoming poor or experiencing misfortune and hardship.
